newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 7.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 7:
WASHINGTON - Defense Secretary William Cohen has decided to reduce planned purchases of jet fighters, shrink the Navy's fleet, cut up to 60,000 servicemen and seek to close more U.S. military bases.
WASHINGTON - The FBI has opened an investigation to determine whether a senior U.S. government official has been passing highly sensitive information to the Israeli government.

WASHINGTON - FBI director Louis Freeh advised Attorney General Janet Reno that early evidence suggesting White House involvement in the Democratic Party fund-raising scandal should warrant the appointment of a special counsel.
WASHINGTON - A military jury sentenced Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson to 25 years in prison for raping six female trainees at the Aberdeen Proving Ground.
DENVER - Timothy McVeigh's sister told a federal jury that a few weeks before the April 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, her brother wrote her that "something big is going to happen."

MEXICO CITY - President Clinton formally opened his first state visit to Mexico with a concerted effort to ease strained relations, acknowledging that the United States must also shoulder blame for the bilateral drug crisis.
WASHINGTON - Virginia attorney general James Gilmore will launch his Republican campaign for governor Thursday.
